intro: Conduit's goal is to be the observability layer a security-conscious team can run next to its AI agents. It should be self-hosted, small enough to audit, and focused on what matters for agents: steps, tools, models, errors and cost.
note: This roadmap is ordered by priority, not by date. Items move as we learn. To suggest a change, open an issue or a PR against `docs/_data/roadmap.json`.

items: mTLS agent identity, with the certificate CommonName as `agent_name`
Per-agent rate limiting, charged per telemetry item
NATS JetStream work queue with at-least-once delivery into ClickHouse
Best-effort export to VictoriaMetrics and Tempo
Span status (ok, error, unset) from end to end, and nanosecond timestamps
Go and Python SDKs: mTLS that trusts only your CA, W3C-sized IDs, status and error recording
Python context that is safe across threads and asyncio tasks
Sign-in: a login form with signed session cookies, or Google Cloud IAP
Trace list: one row per trace, filters by time, agent and errors, keyset paging, agent suggestions
Trace detail: span tree, waterfall timeline, error and LLM details, deep links
`STORE_LLM_PAYLOADS=false` drops prompts and completions at the gateway
`SPAN_RETENTION_DAYS`, with the TTL reconciled on existing tables
`/livez` and `/readyz` on every service, and a `healthcheck` subcommand for scratch images
Compose restart policies and Kubernetes probes, plus GKE IAP manifests
CI: race tests, a generated-code drift check, govulncheck, Docker builds, and a full-stack smoke test with both SDKs
Brand identity, documentation set, and this docs site

items.title: Prompt and completion access control
items.why: Payloads are stored but never shown. Showing them needs a decision on who may see them (see [open decisions](#open-decisions)).

items.title: Schema migrations
items.why: Today `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` runs at startup. Versioned migrations are needed before the schema changes again.

items.title: Metrics and logs ingestion
items.why: `IngestBatch` accepts metrics and logs in the API but rejects them, because there's no pipeline yet.

items.title: Batched, asynchronous SDK delivery
items.why: One blocking RPC per span is simple but slow for chatty agents. Add a buffered exporter with backpressure.

items.title: Read the trace list from `trace_summary`
items.why: Avoid aggregating raw spans for every list query at high volume. Needs root names and agents in the view.

items.title: OpenTelemetry interoperability
items.why: Accept OTLP from existing OpenTelemetry agents, and use OTel semantic conventions for LLM attributes.

items.title: Search
items.why: Search attributes, error messages and span names across traces.

items.title: Published SDKs
items.why: A PyPI package and a tagged Go module with stable import paths (see open decisions).

items.title: Helm chart
items.why: Package the Kubernetes manifests with sensible defaults.

items.title: Cost and token dashboards
items.why: Spend by agent, model and time, built on the existing rollups.

items.title: Alerts
items.why: Error-rate and latency thresholds per agent, with webhook delivery.

items.title: Trace comparison
items.why: Compare two runs of the same task side by side.

items.title: Multi-tenancy
items.why: Separate projects or teams with scoped UI access.

decisions.title: Who can see prompts and completions
Publishing the SDKs
options: Publish to PyPI and as a tagged Go module (needs real module paths instead of `github.com/your-org/...`)

decisions.title: `nats-server` as a test dependency
options: Add an in-process NATS for integration tests
Rely on the compose smoke test, which already covers the path
